title: Exercise Therapy and Physical Activity Modification for Patients With Sever's Disease
official: Exercise Therapy and Physical Activity Modification for Patients With Sever's Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Sever's disease is an overuse injury to the calcaneal growth plate caused by repetitive traction stress from the Achilles tendon in youth. Limited evidence exists to guide effective treatment for Sever's disease and disrupt short- and long-term pain and disability. Exercise therapy has the strongest evidence to promote tissue healing and is supported for other growth plate injuries. This study aims to determine if a comprehensive exercise therapy and activity modification intervention produces a clinically meaningful improvement in (Aim 1) pain and lower extremity function, (Aim 2) muscle and tendon structure, and (Aim 3) physical activity, compared to a non-exercise palliative approach for patients with Sever's disease. Differences between groups after completing 12 weeks of intervention.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Insidious onset of heel pain over several weeks
* Pain on palpation of the calcaneus or Achilles tendon
* Complaint of heel pain with running or jumping activities.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Any underlying condition predisposing heel pain (i.e., spina bifida, osteogenesis imperfecta, Larsen syndrome, cerebral palsy)
* Any other injury that limits their ability to run or jump.
